excluded: reviews/*/packet.md — free prose composed for a human reviewer; no replay assertion reads it
profile.json — the owner's own persona and chrome; a replay needs neither, and an asker-tag duty is decided from the ask's own userId
thread-files/* — attachments, deliberately unredacted where they live and never committable
live/slack/detectives/*/*/*.md — detective briefs and reports, prose quoting what each detective read; the wave's wave.json is carried instead
the composed answer — the record names a path outside the home, or no longer on disk
incident: An inline bot turn was finalised as never-dispatched while its independent reviewer was mid-verdict. Ask CFIXTUREAA/1789521183.332199, 16 Sep 2026: captured 01:13:03.877Z, carded 01:13:12.738Z, and then no 'dispatched' row was EVER written — the loop session composed the answer itself and opened the review straight off the brief and decision files (turn review --brief <file> --decision <file> --answer <file>), which never asks whether a dispatch was recorded. So activeDispatch stayed undefined, every sweep lap printed 'UNROUTED — ROUTE IT NOW' at a turn a session was actively working, and at 01:46:28.759Z the sweep wrote dispatch-failed and finalised the card as abandoned. Round 1 of its review was open at that moment (reviewer workspace:200, spawned 01:26:36.637Z, verdict not written until ~01:49Z, outcome broken). The answer posted at 02:01:07.174Z, fifteen minutes after the card said nobody was coming. RECONSTRUCTED: reviews/<ask>/record.json is round 1's, rebuilt before this freeze ran from the archived round-1 verdict's own filename and body — a review re-open overwrites record.json, so the only file that says a reviewer is open does not survive its round and could not be frozen from the live home.
